attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, asserted in his own voice; the Kahn and Krier quotes are separate and not part of this claim.

semantics.note: Faithful: keeps the evaluative framing, the flat 250,000-page assertion, 'yet' on general lessons, and the 'so far as I have heard' hedge limited to techniques/concepts.

contract.note: Plain reading of 'it is 250,000 pages' as a factual length claim is ordinary; Marcus stated it unhedged. Contract fairly leaves evaluative parts ungraded and protects the awareness-qualified novelty clause. Result turns on treating the page count as literal.

evidence.note: Author's announcement footnote is the apparent source of Marcus's figure; it shows the basis, not a verified length, and says only Lean was presented.

Author's own post, dated Nov 23 (on the evaluation date), says the 250,000+ pages was a joke and only the Lean proof was released. Self-disclosure, but the author is the authoritative source on his own unreleased writeup. Says nothing on lessons or Marcus's awareness.

reviews.rationale: The only unqualified factual component that can be checked, 'it is 250,000 pages', is contradicted: the author says the figure was a joke and only Lean was presented (e2). e1 explains where Marcus got the number but does not verify it. The evaluative parts (useful, innovative, elegant) are ungraded. The general-lessons clause is unresolved. The novelty clause is limited to what Marcus had heard and cannot be graded without evidence of that. Per the contract, the established page-count error supports contradicted.
